text:
micah: Heads-up — saw a steady memory climb on the key-value cache when we run long-context workloads with continuous batching enabled. Not a one-off: reproduced twice on staging.
anya: ugh. any flamegraphs / pprof yet?
micah: grabbed a pprof at the inf-server where it was creeping. main hot path is in the page reclamation and slot-rotation code — reclamation latency spikes when batches merge.
cheng: can you paste the minimal repro? i can spin up a local run.
micah: repro command i used: 
```
./infer_runner --model=gptx-7b --seq-len=4096 --batching=continuous --batch-timeout-ms=20 --trace=kv_pager
```
anyap: saw similar earlier but called it "tail growth". i think reuse windows drift when merges combine heterogeneous sequences.
raj: quick observation from the profile: after a merge we hit a path that scans slots and does a linear reclaim, even when most pages are reusable. that scan latency is what queues subsequent batches.
cheng: can you paste the tiny log snippet?
micah: log excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-12T11:02:03Z] KVPager: merge(batch_id=842, size=12) -> scan_slots=18, reclaimed=2, scan_ms=132
[2026-03-12T11:02:03Z] KVPager: mark_slot_aging slot=5 age=248ms
[2026-03-12T11:02:03Z] Batcher: merged->enqueue delay=140ms head_wait=120ms
```
anya: so merge costs ~130ms then head batch waits 120ms => head-of-queue blocking. we should avoid a full linear scan on merge.
raj: proposed quick fix: change merge path to a sample-based scan + async reclamation. drop full scan threshold to 64 slots. Test in canary?
micah: tried lowering threshold locally to 48 and latency improved on staging repro: head waits reduced from ~120ms to ~15-25ms. memory reclaim per second dropped a bit but stable.
cheng: need to watch fragmentation increase if we reduce reclaim aggressiveness. any fragmentation metric?
micah: fragmentation (unused pages / total pages) ticked up from 6% -> 9% over 10 minutes in that run. not great but not catastrophic.
raj: alternative: keep aggressive reclaim but move it off the merge critical path — spawn reclaim worker and let batch continue, with soft backpressure if reclaim queue grows.
anya: also check kernel selection impact — I noticed when seq>2048 we pick fallback kernels that are slower and hold locks longer. could amplify the blocking.
cheng: good call. i'll add kernel-selection logs to the trace: 
```
KERNEL_SELECT: layer=attn seq=4096 selected=generic_matmul reason=dtype_mismatch
```
micah: exact — fallback kernels triple execution time for large seqs. combined with a heavy merge scan -> queuing.
raj: steps: (1) add async reclaim worker, (2) sample-scan on merge, (3) log kernel selection decisions to metrics, (4) run 4-hour soak on staging with longctx.
anya: i'll open a tiny PR for async reclaim + sample scan. will add feature flag.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: pr/infra/8793 -> staging (canary +0/2)
micah: thanks. last ask — when you run the soak, capture per-batch wait percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and page-fragmentation every minute. we want to track steady-state drift.
cheng: will do. i'll also run a kernel-only ablation to see how much of the head blocking is kernel vs reclaim.
raj: if both contribute, next step is adaptive merge threshold that considers current kernel latency.
micah: cool. assigning follow-ups in thread. :memo:
anya: thx — keeping notes in the perf board. :thumbsup:
